attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is finite-dimensional and valid once the boundary OPE data B and the collar matrix N exist, but Yang-Mills analysis has not yet proved the required boundary OPE for reflected Wilson hairpins, the vanishing/positivity of additive contacts, or Schur-preimage positivity of Q on a dense locked Wilson core.
steps: Start with a finite locked Wilson family F_1,...,F_n and push it off the reflection plane by collars T_{\delta}F_i. Reflection positivity of the regulated lattice/continuum collar construction gives N^{\delta}=[S(\Theta T_{\delta}F_i,T_{\delta}F_j)] >= 0.

Use the RG-to-OS closed-cone bridge only at fixed collar: if every reflected entry converges, then N^{\delta}->N entrywise and N remains positive semidefinite. This part is valid and no longer contains the hard Yang-Mills issue.

Model the collar-collapse boundary OPE as N=B\circ M+C, where M is the intended plane OS matrix, B is a multiplicative boundary anomaly, and C is an additive contact matrix. Diagonal trace continuity gives C_{ii}=0; if C is a positive contact form, Cauchy-Schwarz gives C_{ij}=0, so the remaining obstruction is multiplicative.

Normalize diagonals. Positive diagonal congruence does not affect OS positivity, so the target condition is \widehat M>=0. From N=B\circ M we get \widehat M=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B=:Q. Hence same-theory OS positivity is exactly Q>=0 on the realized finite Wilson family.

For n=3, write Q_{ij}=\rho_{ij}e^{i\phi_{ij}}. The determinant expansion gives 1-\rho_{12}^2-\rho_{23}^2-\rho_{13}^2+2\rho_{12}\rho_{23}\rho_{13}\cos(\phi_{12}+\phi_{23}-\phi_{13}). This exposes the first phase-sensitive falsifier beyond pairwise damping.

If all cycle phase holonomies vanish on the finite support graph, solve \theta_{ij}=\alpha_i-\alpha_j and apply the diagonal unitary D. The problem reduces to checking positive semidefiniteness of the real modulus quotient matrix R. If some cycle holonomy survives, principal minors involving that cycle must be tested directly.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: It gives an exact bridge criterion, not the analytic estimate needed to satisfy it. The missing proof is a same-theory boundary theorem: reflected Wilson collar limits must yield quotient matrices Q that are positive semidefinite for all finite realized families, including triples and higher principal minors.

assumptions: For every finite family F_1,...,F_n in the locked Wilson core, collar approximants T_{\delta}F_i lie in the positive-time test algebra and preserve the reflection operation.
The cutoff-removal topology is valid for each reflected collar matrix entry, so N^{\delta}_{ij} has a continuum collar limit N_{ij}.
Diagonal trace continuity is already proved, and any positive additive boundary contact has zero diagonal; hence Cauchy-Schwarz forces that additive contact to vanish.
The multiplicative anomaly entries B_{ij} are finite and nonzero on the tested finite family, with B_{ii}>0, so normalized Hadamard division is well-defined.
Hermitian conventions are fixed: N_{ji}=\overline{N_{ij}}, B_{ji}=\overline{B_{ij}}, and M_{ji}=\overline{M_{ij}}.
definitions: source object: finite collar-separated reflected Wilson OS matrices N^{\delta}_{ij}=S(\Theta T_{\delta}F_i,T_{\delta}F_j) obtained from regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms and then sent through the RG continuum limit at fixed collar width.
target object: intended continuum same-theory OS matrices M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) for the locked gauge-invariant Wilson/core observable algebra at the reflection plane.

controlled interface: a nonzero multiplicative boundary anomaly matrix B with N=B\circ M after additive contacts have been ruled out, together with normalized matrices \widehat N, \widehat B, \widehat M having unit diagonal.

same-theory condition: M is not allowed to absorb B into a redefined boundary Wilson observable or enlarged boundary algebra; diagonal normalizations may be fixed by the original renormalized observables, but pair-dependent boundary factors must be removed only if the resulting \widehat M remains OS-positive.

equations.label: collar positivity limit
equations.latex: N^{\delta}_{ij}=S(\Theta T_{\delta}F_i,T_{\delta}F_j),\qquad N^{\delta}\ge 0,\qquad N^{\delta}\to N\ \Longrightarrow\ N\ge0
equations.valid_when: The RG-to-OS topology controls the finite reflected collar probes, so the closed cone of positive semidefinite matrices is reached by an actual entrywise limit.

equations.label: boundary anomaly quotient
equations.latex: N=B\circ M,\qquad \widehat M_{ij}=\frac{\widehat N_{ij}}{\widehat B_{ij}}=:Q_{ij},\qquad \widehat M\ge0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Q\ge0
equations.valid_when: Additive contacts vanish, B has no zero entries on the finite family, and diagonal congruences from normalization are same-theory allowed.

equations.label: phase holonomy obstruction
equations.valid_when: The quotient matrix Q is normalized Hermitian and all three tested off-diagonal entries are nonzero; H_{ijk} is invariant under diagonal unitary rephasing of observables.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A single finite Wilson family with N >= 0 but Q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B not positive semidefinite is a valid same-theory falsifier of the collar-to-plane OS bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma replaces the earlier overstrong rank-one-boundary claim with an exact finite-matrix bridge. It says what must be shown for the same theory: not B=1 universally, but Q >= 0 on the realized locked Wilson cone.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite quotient-holonomy boundary bridge: for any finite locked Wilson family whose collar OS matrices converge, same-theory OS positivity after collar collapse is equivalent to positivity of the normalized Hadamard quotient by the boundary anomaly matrix. The closed-cone step gives the collar limit N >= 0; the nonformal Yang-Mills content is proving that Q = \widehat N \oslash \widehat B is positive semidefinite on every realized finite family, not merely proving that B is close to trivial.

assumptions: 0<=\rho_{ij}<=1 for each pair, so every 2-by-2 principal minor of Q is nonnegative.
The three off-diagonal quotient entries are nonzero; zero entries are handled by deleting the corresponding edge in the support graph.
The target same-theory OS form for this triple is represented by Q up to positive diagonal congruence.
definitions: normalized quotient: Q_{ii}=1 and Q_{ij}=\rho_{ij}e^{i\phi_{ij}} for i\ne j, where Q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B.
realized triple: three Wilson collar observables for which both the collar matrix N and boundary anomaly B are computed from the same locked gauge-invariant algebra.

equations.label: three-by-three determinant
equations.valid_when: Q is a normalized Hermitian 3-by-3 quotient matrix.

equations.label: phase falsifier inequality
equations.valid_when: The quotient Q is the actual same-theory plane matrix after removing the multiplicative boundary anomaly from the collar limit.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a boundary OPE calculation produces this negative determinant while N remains positive, then pairwise checks were misleading and the same-theory OS passage fails for that triple.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: It gives a concrete finite determinant experiment for the next Yang-Mills calculation: compute N and B for a reflected Wilson triple and test the quotient determinant.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Three-hairpin determinant falsifier: the first phase-sensitive obstruction is already visible in a normalized 3-by-3 quotient matrix, where pairwise damping tests can all pass but the determinant can still be negative.

assumptions: Q is Hermitian with unit diagonal and nonzero entries on the chosen support graph edges.
The graph is treated componentwise; isolated vertices are automatically positive.
Allowed rephasings are diagonal unitary congruences of the same finite observable span and do not change the underlying Schwinger functions.
definitions: support graph: vertices are observables F_i and an edge ij is present when Q_{ij}\ne0.
cycle holonomy: the sum of quotient phases around an oriented cycle, invariant under rephasing F_i by unit complex scalars.
modulus quotient matrix: R_{ii}=1 and R_{ij}=|Q_{ij}| on the support graph after all quotient phases have been gauged away.

equations.label: coboundary condition
equations.valid_when: The quotient phases are defined on a finite graph of nonzero quotient entries.

equations.label: phase removal
equations.valid_when: The coboundary condition holds on the connected component under consideration.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A nonzero triangle holonomy is not automatically fatal, but it is the first phase falsifier candidate; it becomes fatal exactly when the corresponding principal minor of Q turns negative.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: It splits the Yang-Mills boundary problem into a cohomological phase test followed by a real principal-minor test.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Phase-coboundary reduction: on a finite support graph of nonzero quotient entries, quotient phases are harmless exactly when every cycle holonomy vanishes; then a diagonal unitary congruence removes all phases and the remaining obstruction is real modulus positivity.

control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves additive contact elimination plus vanishing quotient holonomy and modulus quotient PSD on a dense Wilson core, or equivalently proves Q>=0 for every finite realized boundary OPE matrix.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a sharper, non-tautological bridge criterion: finite quotient-holonomy positivity. It preserves the valid closed-cone result while identifying the next Yang-Mills estimate as boundary OPE control for reflected Wilson triples and higher finite families.

dependency_updates.description: The locked Wilson core must be rich enough to realize finite quotient tests, especially triples, without changing the observable algebra at the reflection plane.
The topology must control mixed reflected Wilson products and their collar-collapse limits, not only individual Schwinger distributions or pairwise entries.
dependency_updates.status: open; now testable by finite matrix convergence.

dependency_updates.description: Need existence and estimates for N=B\circ M+C, vanishing or positive-zero-diagonal control of C, and PSD of Q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B on realized finite families.

falsifiers: A three-hairpin Wilson calculation with N>=0 but det(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B)<0 is a concrete falsifier of same-theory OS positivity after collar collapse.
A nonzero additive boundary contact C with zero diagonal but not positive as a contact form would falsify the reduction from N=B\circ M+C to the pure multiplicative quotient model.
A quotient phase triangle with negative determinant shows that pairwise damping bounds are not a valid substitute for finite OS positivity.
If the RG cutoff-removal topology controls single Wilson loops but not mixed reflected triple products, then the closed-cone-to-quotient derivation is not valid for the needed test algebra.

If the anomaly B is absorbed by redefining the boundary Wilson algebra, the positivity statement may be true for a modified theory but is a same-theory falsifier for the intended Yang-Mills Schwinger functions.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 205 learned that the post-collar bridge is an exact Schur-preimage problem on realized Wilson OS matrices. The valid closed-cone argument supplies N>=0, but same-theory positivity is precisely Q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B>=0 after additive contacts are eliminated. This is stronger than pairwise damping and weaker than demanding B be rank one universally. The first useful falsifier is a three-hairpin determinant with quotient phase holonomy; if phases are coboundaries, the remaining task is real modulus PSD for all principal minors. The branch has therefore moved from topology naming to a concrete boundary OPE computation program.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the leading boundary OPE for three reflected Wilson hairpin collars with a shared reflection-plane footprint. Extract \widehat B, \widehat N, the quotient holonomy \Phi, and det(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B). A negative determinant is the next falsifier; zero holonomy plus positive modulus minors would support promotion to a finite-family same-theory OS bridge.
